title: FileSystemHandle picker grants die on browser restart — service worker cannot re-request them; re-grant must happen in an extension page with user activation
trigger: A stored FileSystemHandle (IndexedDB) is read from the service worker or any context other than the page that picked it, especially after a browser restart
principle: File handles obtained via showOpenFilePicker/drag-drop keep implicit 'granted' read permission only for the browser session — after restart queryPermission() returns 'prompt' and getFile() throws 'not allowed by the user agent'. A service worker can call requestPermission() but it silently returns 'prompt' (no UI possible); an offscreen document throws 'User activation is required'. Only a real extension page (popup/options) with transient activation can re-request — and on extension origins it auto-grants silently. Explicit requestPermission grants persist across restarts, so one re-grant fixes the handle permanently. Guard the request with navigator.userActivation.isActive — calling it without activation blocks on a native prompt. Verify via CDP Browser.resetPermissions + SW probe to reproduce the 'prompt' state deterministically.

cases.context: Local Forvo audio: handles picked in Settings panel were stored in IndexedDB and read by the service worker via FETCH_LOCAL_AUDIO. After Quetta restarted, SW-side verifyPermission returned 'prompt'→ requestPermission no-op → resolver null → provider silently returned [] → orchestrator fell back to Wiktionary while everything looked configured (green dot, 285k index).

applyFor: Any feature that persists FileSystemHandle in IndexedDB and reads it from a service worker, offscreen document, or after a browser restart
Local-file-backed providers (audio, video, dictionaries) that silently fall back on permission failure
Designing 'remember this file' UX — plan a gesture-path re-grant, never rely on the SW to prompt
